The observed failures that the spec has not yet explained.

```text
Lists the failures that HAPPENED (ingested with 'anchors ingest --logs') and
that carry no conclusion in the spec yet.

A spec declares a failure as POSSIBLE without knowing how it will happen — an
`if x == null` foresees the failure without knowing where the null comes from.
Once the application runs, the log has the context that answers it.

Three conclusions, and all three are progress:

  cause found    write it beside the rule — the handling can stop being generic
  resilient      `@resilient: <reason>` — it leaves the radar without leaving the record
  still unknown  `@observing: <what was ruled out>` — different from nobody having looked

The third is what no observability tool records, and it is knowledge: the next person to
look starts from what was already ruled out, instead of from zero.
```

## Usage

```bash
anchors failures [flags]
```

## Flags

| Flag | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--all` |  | also list the failures that already carry a conclusion (resilient or under observation) |
| `--map` |  | path to the map |
| `--root` | `.` | project root |

## Confronting the project — family

Commands of the same family — what tells each apart:

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`anchors check`](/docs/cli/commands/check/) | Run the quality gates (the pipeline) |
| [`anchors verify`](/docs/cli/commands/verify/) | Run EVERYTHING the phase requires: Anchors gates + external tools |
| [`anchors coverage`](/docs/cli/commands/coverage/) | Show coverage by scenario, by line, of the DIFF and the delta |
| [`anchors stale`](/docs/cli/commands/stale/) | List stale edges — what changed and has not been reconfronted |
| [`anchors impact`](/docs/cli/commands/impact/) | Impact analysis: what a change to this file reaches |
| **`anchors failures`** | The observed failures that the spec has not yet explained |
